descriptionChirho: Adjective καθαρός denoting cleanliness or purity in both ritual/ceremonial and moral/spiritual senses. Used of persons who are clean/pure (John 13:10-11, 15:3; Acts 18:6, 20:26), of conscience and heart (1 Tim 1:5, 3:9; 2 Tim 1:3, 2:22; Titus 1:15), of pure religion (Jas 1:27), of pure gold/glass (Rev 21:18, 21), and of clean linen (Rev 15:6, 19:8, 19:14). All three clusters converge on the same translations: eng 'clean/pure', spa 'limpio/puro', hin शुद्ध, arb طَاهِرُونَ/نَقِيٌّ, kor 깨끗한/순수한, swa 'safi'. The separation into three clusters reflects only inflectional variation (gender, number, case), not distinct lexicographic senses.
